minutes.summary: The town manager presented the five-year financial forecast and the fiscal 2020 capital plan. why_it_matters: The forecast shows a deficit in the later years because free cash is not projected past FY20, so those years depend on revenue or spending choices not yet made.

The capital plan is paid from tax revenue, free cash, unexpended capital and bond premium, so what the town buys and how it pays can affect future tax bills and the borrowing a Town Meeting vote may be asked to approve.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee heard the five-year forecast, which shows a deficit in FY21 to FY23 because free cash is not projected beyond FY20. No vote was taken.
The committee heard the FY20 capital plan, funded from tax revenue, free cash, unexpended capital and bond premium. No vote was taken.
The DPW fuel tank project needs more money because it is moving to engineered plans and outsourcing.
A resident objected to the town manager's power to amend the capital plan, and spoke on that power under the Charter.
The December 13 minutes were deferred. The next meeting is Feb 14 for the town manager's budget, with department presentations Feb 21.
